claims.text: MoNbTaVW refractory high-entropy alloys exhibit anomalous thermoelastic softening and mechanical response at high temperatures.
The high-temperature thermoelastic and mechanical behavior of MoNbTaVW is primarily governed by grain-boundary-mediated processes.
A fine-grained microstructure has greater grain-boundary density than a coarse-grained microstructure.
Increased grain-boundary density enhances grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
Increased grain-boundary density enhances diffusional processes at high temperature.
Grain boundaries provide sites at which strain can be accommodated.
Enhanced grain-boundary sliding and diffusion reduce the effective thermoelastic modulus.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation alters yield behavior relative to coarse-grained material.
High-pressure torsion followed by controlled annealing can produce distinct fine- and coarse-grained MoNbTaVW microstructures.
Rapid thermal cycling or minor alloying additions can stabilize the fine-grained MoNbTaVW structure at high temperatures.
Grain-boundary sliding and diffusion are activated in MoNbTaVW over 900–1300 °C.
Maintaining stable grain sizes during testing is necessary for attributing response differences to grain-boundary density.
Dislocation-mediated mechanisms may operate concurrently with the proposed grain-boundary processes.
Fine-grained MoNbTaVW samples will have a lower effective thermoelastic modulus than coarse-grained samples under otherwise identical high-temperature testing.
Fine-grained MoNbTaVW samples will exhibit a discernibly different yield-stress response from coarse-grained samples.
Failure to observe a statistically significant modulus reduction or a discernible yield-response difference in the fine-grained samples would falsify the proposed grain-boundary mechanism.
